che-lam-thach-xa.name: Thach Xa Che Lam
aliases: Thach Xa ginger and molasses rice cake
che-lam-thach-xa.serving_basis: About 24 chewy pieces served with hot tea.
che-lam-thach-xa.description: Che lam from Thach Xa is a Xu Doai sweet made with toasted glutinous rice flour, sugarcane molasses, ginger and roasted peanuts. Bếp Việt has edited a small home batch with a balanced chew and gentle warmth; it is not presented as an artisan household’s exact formula.
che-lam-thach-xa.finished_dish: Chewy, firm pieces lightly dusted with rice flour; molasses sweetness is balanced by warm ginger and nutty peanuts.
che-lam-thach-xa.excerpt: A chewy Xu Doai rice sweet with molasses, ginger and roasted peanuts.
che-lam-thach-xa.serving: Let the cake cool completely, cut into bite-size pieces and serve with green or hot tea.
tips: Add toasted rice flour gradually so the mixture stays chewy rather than dry and crumbly.
Cook molasses over low heat, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
Fold in the peanuts last to keep them crisp.
che-lam-thach-xa.tip: Add toasted rice flour gradually so the mixture stays chewy.
che-lam-thach-xa.image_alt: Thach Xa che lam cut into square pieces dusted with rice flour and dotted with roasted peanuts, ginger and molasses, isolated on transparent background.

ingredients.name: Toasted glutinous rice flour
ingredients.notes: Toast gently until fragrant, cool and sift.

ingredients.name: Sugarcane molasses
ingredients.notes: Use thick molasses without a burnt taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely grate or mince.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Remove skins; leave whole or coarsely crush.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil
ingredients.notes: Lightly grease the tray and knife.

ingredients.name: Toasted glutinous rice flour
ingredients.notes: For dusting while shaping and cutting.

preparation_steps: Roast the peanuts until fragrant, rub off the skins, and prepare a flat parchment-lined tray.
Toast the glutinous rice flour in a dry pan over low heat until fragrant and free-flowing; let it cool.
Sift the dusting flour and lightly oil the tray and knife.
cooking_steps: Put molasses and ginger in a heavy saucepan. Heat gently until simmering and fragrant.
Lower the heat. Add toasted rice flour gradually, stirring briskly with a wooden spoon until a cohesive, pliable dough pulls slightly from the pan.
Fold in the peanuts. Transfer the dough to the tray and press it into a slab about 2 cm thick.
Cool completely, dust lightly with rice flour and cut into squares. Store airtight in a cool, dry place.
che-lam-thach-xa.time_note: About 1 hour, including cooling before cutting.

targets.instruction: Reduce molasses and flour proportionally; stop heating once the dough comes together.
Divide the dough into two portions for easier kneading and shaping.
Shape two separate slabs; keep molasses warm and fold peanuts into each batch.

editorial.variant_note: A home-size adaptation based on ingredients and local che lam identity reported by a Hanoi source; ratios are Bếp Việt editorial work, not an artisan household standard.
needs: Test chew and storage time with different molasses brands before publication.

khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.name: Ha Tinh Khoai Xeo
aliases: Ha Tinh dried sweet potato and sticky rice
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.serving_basis: One pot of chewy, nutty khoai xeo for four people.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.description: Khoai xeo is a rustic Ha Tinh dish made with dried sweet potato, sticky rice, beans and peanuts. Bếp Việt has edited a home method that soaks dry beans first, then gently mashes the cooked mixture so it stays chewy and textured.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.finished_dish: Soft dried sweet potato and sticky rice combine with beans and peanuts for a gently sweet, nutty dish that is not mushy.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.excerpt: A comforting Ha Tinh pot of dried sweet potato, sticky rice, beans and peanuts.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.serving: Serve warm as breakfast or a snack; add a little sesame-peanut salt if desired.
tips: Soak dry beans and cook until tender before adding the rice.
Keep the water just level with the ingredients after adding rice; add hot water little by little if needed.
Mash lightly while hot, leaving some sweet potato pieces and beans intact.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.tip: Soak dry beans first so they cook through before the sticky rice is done.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.image_alt: Ha Tinh khoai xeo, a golden-brown chewy mix of dried sweet potato, sticky rice, red and black beans and peanuts in a rustic bowl, isolated on transparent background.

ingredients.name: Dried sweet potato
ingredients.notes: Choose clean, mold-free slices; rinse quickly and drain.

ingredients.name: Sticky rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Dried red beans
ingredients.notes: Pick over, rinse and soak for 6–8 hours.

ingredients.name: Dried black beans
ingredients.notes: Pick over, rinse and soak for 6–8 hours.

ingredients.name: Raw peanuts
ingredients.notes: Rinse briefly; roasted peanuts may be folded in at the end instead.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the potatoes’ natural sweetness.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly to balance sweetness.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Barely cover the ingredients; add hot water if needed.

preparation_steps: Pick over and rinse the red and black beans, soak in clean water for 6–8 hours, then drain.
Rinse the sticky rice. Rinse the dried sweet potato quickly to remove dust; do not soak it until soft.
Prepare a heavy-bottomed pot and keep hot water ready for topping up.
cooking_steps: Put the sweet potato, beans, peanuts and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer 25–30 minutes until the beans are nearly tender.
Add sticky rice and stir once. Simmer gently 15–20 minutes until the rice is cooked and most liquid is absorbed. Add a little hot water if needed.
Season with salt and sugar, stir gently, cover and rest 10 minutes.
Lightly mash with a wooden spoon while warm. Leave some potato pieces and beans intact; serve warm.
khoai-xeo-ha-tinh.time_note: About 7 hours 10 minutes, mostly for soaking the beans; soak them overnight if convenient.

targets.instruction: Start with 500–600 ml water and add more during cooking if needed.
Use a wide pot so ingredients cook evenly; lower the heat after adding rice.
Cook in two batches if the pot is not large; add sugar after the rice is tender.

editorial.variant_note: This home version soaks dried beans first for reliable tenderness. The local article confirms the dish name, core ingredients and mashing action, but not the soaking step.
needs: Test water and timing with locally available dried sweet potato and bean varieties.

mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.name: Yen Tu Bamboo Shoots Stir-Fried with Beef
aliases: Yen Tu bamboo shoot and beef stir-fry
Quang Ninh bamboo shoots with beef
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.serving_basis: One plate of bamboo shoots and beef for four, served with rice.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.description: Firm Yen Tu bamboo shoots have a lightly bitter, nutty character and are commonly stir-fried with beef, garlic and seasoning. Bếp Việt has edited a home version that cooks fresh bamboo shoots thoroughly first and keeps the beef tender.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.finished_dish: Crisp-tender bamboo shoots carry gentle bitterness and sweetness; just-cooked beef is coated with garlic fragrance and a light pan sauce.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.excerpt: A quick Quang Ninh stir-fry of Yen Tu bamboo shoots, beef and garlic.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.serving: Serve immediately with steamed rice; fresh washed greens may accompany it as in local meals.
tips: Fresh bamboo shoots must be prepared and boiled thoroughly before stir-frying; never taste them raw.
Quickly sear the beef in a hot pan, remove it, and return it at the end to keep it tender.
Season lightly because the pan juices concentrate as they reduce.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.tip: Boil fresh bamboo shoots thoroughly before stir-frying.
search_terms: Yen Tu bamboo shoots with beef
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.image_alt: Yen Tu bamboo shoots stir-fried with tender beef slices and garlic, served on a ceramic plate, isolated on transparent background.

ingredients.name: Fresh bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Wash, split or slice, boil thoroughly and change the water if bitterness remains.

ingredients.name: Beef tenderloin
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly across the grain.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel, crush and mince.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil
ingredients.notes: Divide between the beef and bamboo shoots.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season to taste.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Optional; omit for a lighter flavor.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Finish with pepper.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For boiling the bamboo shoots if needed.

preparation_steps: Rinse the shoots, remove tough outer layers and split or slice. Boil 15 minutes, discard the water and rinse; if still bitter, boil again in fresh water.
Slice the beef across the grain. Marinate 10 minutes with half the garlic, fish sauce, oyster sauce and a little pepper.
Drain the boiled shoots well and heat a wide pan.
cooking_steps: Heat a little oil. Stir-fry the beef over high heat for 1–2 minutes until it just changes color, then transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil and garlic. When fragrant, add the shoots and stir-fry 3–4 minutes until hot and lightly firm. Season with the remaining fish sauce.
Return the beef and toss for 30–60 seconds. Taste, add pepper and turn off the heat.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-thit-bo.time_note: About 50 minutes, including 10 minutes to marinate the beef and prepare the shoots.

targets.example: Yen Tu Bamboo Shoots Stir-Fried with Beef for 2
targets.instruction: Scale down the main ingredients and begin with half the seasoning, adjusting after cooking.

targets.example: Yen Tu Bamboo Shoots Stir-Fried with Beef for 6
targets.instruction: Stir-fry in two rounds so the pan stays hot and the beef remains tender.

targets.example: Yen Tu Bamboo Shoots Stir-Fried with Beef for 8
targets.instruction: Use a large pan or cook in two batches; return the beef just before serving.

editorial.variant_note: A home adaptation of the Yen Tu regional dish identified by Vietnam News Agency; Bếp Việt adds household measurements and thorough boiling instructions for fresh shoots.
needs: Confirm sourcing and seasonal differences in fresh shoots; test boiling time by shoot maturity.

canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.name: Thai-Style Canh Ot from Western Nghe An
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.serving_basis: One lightly thickened chicken and rice soup for four people.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.description: Canh ột is a rice-and-herb soup of Thai communities in western Nghe An, with variations named for their main ingredient. Bếp Việt has edited a chicken version for home cooking with young banana pith, lemongrass and soaked, coarsely pounded rice; it is not claimed as a universal village recipe.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.finished_dish: The soup is lightly thickened by softened rice, with tender chicken, delicate young banana pith and fragrant lemongrass.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.excerpt: A home-edited chicken version of the Thai rice soup from western Nghe An.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.serving: Serve hot with rice or as the main soup in a meal; offer chili salt separately.
tips: Soak and coarsely pound the rice so it thickens the soup without forming lumps.
Cook the chicken fully before adding rice; stir the bottom of the pot as the rice softens.
Use clean young banana pith, remove mature layers and soak briefly in lightly salted water.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.tip: Add the pounded rice gradually while stirring so the soup stays smooth.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.image_alt: A bowl of lightly thickened western Nghe An canh ot chicken soup with young banana pith, lemongrass and herbs, isolated on transparent background.

ingredients.name: Bone-in chicken
ingredients.notes: Cut into pieces, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: White rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse, soak for at least 2 hours, then pound or pulse to coarse cracked grains.

ingredients.name: Young banana pith
ingredients.notes: Remove mature layers, slice thinly and soak briefly in lightly salted water.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise the stalks; slice a little tender leaf if available.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice or bruise.

ingredients.name: Young mac khen leaves or fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Optional; rinse and chop.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use skimmed chicken broth if preferred.

preparation_steps: Rinse the rice and soak in clean water for about 2 hours. Drain and pound or pulse to cracked grains, not fine flour.
Clean and cut the chicken. Peel mature layers from the young banana pith, slice thinly, soak in lightly salted water for 10 minutes and rinse.
Bruise the lemongrass and ginger; rinse and drain any herbs.
cooking_steps: Put chicken, water, lemongrass and ginger in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim and simmer about 20 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Add the young banana pith and cook 5–7 minutes until just tender. Season with salt.
Sprinkle in the cracked rice gradually while stirring to prevent lumps. Simmer 15–20 minutes until the rice softens and the soup thickens lightly.
Turn off the heat, add optional herbs, taste and serve hot.
canh-ot-mien-tay-nghe-an.time_note: About 3 hours 10 minutes, including the rice soak.

targets.example: Thai-Style Canh Ot from Western Nghe An for 2
targets.instruction: Cook a smaller pot, starting with half the salt and adjusting to taste.

targets.example: Thai-Style Canh Ot from Western Nghe An for 6
targets.instruction: Use a wide pot and stir gently after adding rice so it softens evenly.

targets.example: Thai-Style Canh Ot from Western Nghe An for 8
targets.instruction: Divide chicken and broth between two pots if needed; add rice last to control thickness.

editorial.variant_note: This home recipe selects a chicken variation that local coverage confirms exists. Young banana pith and herbs are not presented as mandatory in every version of canh ột.
needs: Test rice texture and soup thickness; verify local herb names and suitable substitutions.

ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.name: Song Giang Grilled Ca Mat
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.serving_basis: One plate of grilled ca mat for four people, served with rice and greens.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.description: Ca mat from the Song Giang River is associated with Muong Qua in western Nghe An. Local reporting describes gentle cleaning followed by grilling, frying, boiling or braising; Bếp Việt has edited a simple grilled home version and does not claim it is the only traditional or ceremonial recipe.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.finished_dish: The fish is fully cooked with lightly charred skin, firm sweet flesh and a fragrant aroma.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.excerpt: A simple home-style grilled Song Giang river fish with chili salt.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, boiled greens and a small bowl of green chili salt.
tips: Choose fresh fish, keep it chilled and prepare it shortly before cooking.
Grill over medium heat and turn gently to cook evenly without breaking the fish.
Cook until the thickest part is opaque and fully done; do not serve raw or undercooked fish.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.tip: Grill over medium heat and turn gently so the fish stays intact.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.image_alt: Whole Song Giang ca mat grilled until lightly golden, served with green chili and herbs, isolated on a transparent background.

ingredients.name: Fresh ca mat fish
ingredients.notes: Choose intact, medium-sized fish and keep chilled until preparation.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For a light seasoning and dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Green chili
ingredients.notes: Grill or pound with salt for a dip.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Juice, to taste.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil
ingredients.notes: Brush a very thin film on the clean grill.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs and greens
ingredients.notes: Wash thoroughly and drain; serve alongside.

preparation_steps: Keep the fish chilled. Rinse gently, clean the gills and, for larger fish, remove the entrails; drain well.
Rub a light coating of salt over the fish and rest for 10 minutes; avoid a long marinade that could overpower its natural flavor.
Wash and drain the greens. Clean and preheat the grill.
cooking_steps: Grill over glowing charcoal or in an oven preheated to 200°C. Turn gently after 6–8 minutes and continue until the thickest part is opaque and flakes from the bone.
Pound green chili with a little salt; add a few drops of lime if desired.
Serve the fish hot with greens and rice. Check carefully for bones while eating.
ca-mat-nuong-song-giang.time_note: About 50 minutes, including a 10-minute light seasoning rest.

targets.example: Song Giang Grilled Ca Mat for 2
targets.instruction: Grill a smaller batch, keep the fish seasoning light and season the dipping salt separately.

targets.example: Song Giang Grilled Ca Mat for 6
targets.instruction: Use a wide grill or cook in two rounds so the fish is easy to turn.

targets.example: Song Giang Grilled Ca Mat for 8
targets.instruction: Use two grills or cook in rounds to maintain steady heat; do not stack the fish.

editorial.variant_note: A simple home grilling method based on local reports of ca mat and regional cooking options; it is not asserted to represent a ceremonial recipe or the only Thai community version.
needs: Verify seasonal local naming and typical fish size; test grilling times by fish size before release.
